Every public type and method names the clause it implements (EC-n, EC-Jn, DA-n, CS-n, DS-n, C2 section n).

risks: Spring Boot's fat-jar launcher and Class.forName: use the thread context class loader (Boot's LaunchedClassLoader) when resolving the role class, or the worker class will not be found at runtime even though it is in BOOT-INF/lib.
Doing draft registration and job admission in two transactions, leaving orphan DRAFT rows on refusal.
Returning camelCase keys the frontend does not read.
Editing an architecture or manifests assertion instead of fixing the arrangement -- forbidden; ask on the relay instead.

in: Routes. Replace or extend DeviceRegistrationController so that it serves exactly what the frontend calls and remove it from the component-scan exclusion (SessionAdminController stays excluded). POST /devices/add-single takes {address, vendor, credential_reference_id}; the service derives transport_kind from vendor (Check Point -> ssh_exec, Palo Alto -> pan_xml_api; any other vendor -> 422 VALIDATION_FAILED vendor_hint_invalid), registers the DRAFT device through DeviceRegistrationService (is_test_target false, address as address_ref), then admits the vendor's confirm capability through JobAdmissionService with client idempotency key equal to the device id and the actor from the gate, all in ONE transaction boundary so a refused admission leaves no orphan DRAFT row; response 200 {device_id, job_id, enrollment_state: DRAFT}; an admission refusal maps to 409 {error: ADMISSION_REFUSED, code, reason} with the draft rolled back. GET /devices/{id} returns the DeviceDetail shape above (404 {error: NOT_FOUND} when unknown), with job = the most recent job whose target is this device or null. GET /devices returns every device (add a DeviceRepository list method, jOOQ implementation, ordered by creation) as DeviceSummary rows. Role gating follows the existing convention: POST requires the role that DEVICE_REGISTER already requires; the two GETs require any authenticated session with device read access as the other read controllers do. Write the JSON keys exactly as the frontend types spell them.

Composition. Wire JobAdmissionService (CapabilityRegistry, PersistenceDeviceEnrollmentReadPort, job record dao, transaction boundary) as a Spring bean next to the existing repositories in the service composition root; wire the new device read/list beans. Add service tests: add-single happy path (draft written and job admitted with the right capability id per vendor), refusal rolls the draft back, unknown vendor 422, GET detail shape with and without facts, GET list shape. Use the fakes the existing service tests use; no database in unit tests.

Worker packaging. Add com.securityexpert.nexus.ui2.platform.launch.Ui2Launcher (platform-core) whose main takes args[0] as the workload role: service -> Class.forName("com.securityexpert.nexus.ui2.service.boot.Ui2Application") main(remaining args); worker -> Class.forName("com.securityexpert.nexus.ui2.worker.Ui2WorkerMain") main(remaining args); missing or unknown role -> print one line to stderr and exit 2. Unit-test the dispatch with a stub role table. In ui2/service/build.gradle.kts set the Spring Boot mainClass to Ui2Launcher and add runtimeOnly(project(":worker")) with a comment naming this packet's decision and DIR-2; Ui2Application itself is unchanged and stays the Spring @SpringBootApplication. Confirm with the built jar that `java -jar service-boot.jar worker` reaches Ui2WorkerMain (it may exit early for missing env; the exit path must be Ui2WorkerMain's, not a ClassNotFoundException) and that `java -jar service-boot.jar service` still boots Spring (the existing boot test or a smoke start with a missing DB that fails in the DataSource, not in class loading). Containerfile: no change is expected; if one is needed, ENTRYPOINT still starts with java and CMD stays exactly ["service"].

Both vendors in one worker. Give Ui2WorkerMain a composite DeviceTransport that routes by the endpoint's transport_kind: ssh_exec -> SshExecTransport with the store-backed SSH resolver, pan_xml_api -> PanXmlApiTransport with the store-backed PAN resolver; unit-test the routing and that an unknown transport kind fails closed with a terminal step failure, never a fallback to the other transport. Ui2WorkerMain reads no new secret; trust-rule env names stay as they are.

Manifests. deploy/ui2/52-worker-deployment.yaml and 50-service-deployment.yaml keep the same image reference; if the worker needs any env var the service does not, declare it there and extend tests/test_ui2_deployment_manifests.py accordingly. Run that test file.
Frontend: no change expected. If a route response shape and adminApi.ts disagree, change the SERVICE to match the frontend, not the reverse.

recommended_reasoning.reason: The remaining gap is real-environment observation against a live database and (ideally) real or containerized devices, not new design work -- a lighter tier than this movement's own (which combined a transaction-boundary design, Spring Boot class-loading and a new transport-routing class).

unresolved_risks: AC-1's jOOQ-nested-transaction rollback (draft write + job admission sharing one outer transaction via savepoints) is proved here only by a unit-level TransactionBoundary fake that simulates rollback; it has not been proved against a real PostgreSQL connection. A future movement with integration-tests in scope should add a real-DB test asserting that a refused add-single leaves zero rows in devices/endpoints.

DeviceCompositionConfiguration's confirmCapabilityRegistry() duplicates worker's ConfirmCapabilities placeholder builder (both build the same two gate-free, CAP_OFFLINE capabilities from CapabilitySpec literals) because service may never import a worker class (DIR-2). The two builders must be kept in sync by hand if either capability's id/vendor/transport ever changes; a later movement replacing this whole placeholder pattern with a real spec-file-driven capability registry (noted as future work in worker's own ConfirmCapabilities javadoc already) would remove this duplication in one pass.

GateChainInterceptor's new one-segment wildcard route matching ("GET /devices/*") is generic (any future path-variable route can reuse it) but is exercised today only by GET /devices/{id}; it has no dedicated unit test of its own (only end-to-end coverage through the existing DeviceRegistrationGateTest-style tests, which this movement did not add a new one for since the routing change itself is mechanical and the gate behavior per action id is already covered by ActionRegistry's own semantics).
